_note: Phase 5 corrections to contested-verse handling, applied by scripts/apply_phase5_patches.py so they survive a knowledge rebuild. Two problems found in audit: BG_4_8 carried contested=true with an EMPTY pluralism_note (a silent stub on exactly the path that needs care), and BG_11_33 — the nimitta/instrument verse, historically the most misused verse in the Gita — was not marked contested at all.

BG_4_8.pluralism_note: Read cosmically (periodic avatara) by Gaudiya and many bhakti schools, and ethically/allegorically (the restoration of right order within a person and a society) by Advaita and modern readings. Never present as a forecast that rescue is coming, and never as licence to appoint oneself the punisher of the 'wicked'.

BG_11_33.pluralism_note: Arjuna is told he is already an instrument in an outcome larger than himself. This is the single most misused verse in the Gita: it is not a licence for violence, not a claim that any harm one causes was 'meant to be', and not permission to surrender moral responsibility. Traditions differ on how much agency nimitta leaves the actor — present it as the humility of acting without owning the fruit, never as fatalism.
